data: Iran's orbital launch site: Safir put Omid, Iran's first home-built satellite, in orbit in 2009

Iran's main spaceport, 50 km southeast of Semnan, operated by the Iranian Space Agency; it includes an older circular pad used by Safir and the larger Imam Khomeini Space Launch Terminal used by Simorgh. The first Safir orbital attempt, with a dummy satellite, was on 17 August 2008, and Omid reached orbit on 2 February 2009. Facts from Wikipedia (Semnan Space Center, Safir, Omid) and the IISS analysis of October 2026; coordinates are the Semnan Space Center point on Wikipedia (the Safir pad area).
Iran's Simorgh rocket falls short of orbit with three payloads aboard — NASASpaceFlight

Semnan Space Center lies about 50 km southeast of the city of Semnan, in the northern Dasht-e Kavir desert; the Iranian Space Agency runs it. Its oldest pad is a 65 m circular platform with a service tower, used by the Safir rocket. A Safir flew from Semnan on 17 August 2008 with a dummy satellite, and on 2 February 2009 it put the 40 cm cube Omid into orbit, making Iran the ninth country to launch its own satellite. A larger complex to the east, the Imam Khomeini Space Launch Terminal, has a rail-mounted service tower for the bigger Simorgh, which first flew on 19 April 2016. Airstrikes on 24 to 26 March 2026 damaged or destroyed four structures around the Simorgh complex, according to an IISS analysis of satellite imagery; no launch from Semnan has followed.
